text:
maria: FYI - after the EU GPU pool migration window (~00:50-01:10 UTC) we're seeing apiserver watch_queue_depth explode on the eu cluster and controller-manager reconcile latency climb. Provisioning paths returning 503s intermittently. Any eyes?

kai: Looking now. Which metrics are worst?

maria: watch_queue_depth ~9k on apiserver-eu, apiserver_request_latencies 95p jumped to ~1.2s, etcd follower_lag spikes ~400-600ms, controller-manager workqueue growing. Logs show repeated watch reconnects from gpu-provisioner.

oliver: We pushed the "packed placement" policy at ~00:50 to reduce idle GPUs. That increases attach/detach churn when nodes are drained. Did the rollout change controller resync or lease durations?

tessa: We did not change lease durations, just placement logic. The rollout triggered lots of moves as expected.

maria: Short-term mitigation: pause further GPU migrations and throttle provisioner fanout. I know that hurts utilization but stabilizes control plane.

kai: Ops knobs: 1) scale down provisioner replicas, 2) restart controller-manager with lower --kube-api-qps/--kube-api-burst, 3) consider increasing watch-cache bucket counts for the hot-key resources.

oliver: Will scale down provisioner and do a controlled restart of controller-manager.

tessa: Running now:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/gpu-provisioner --replicas=1
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deploy/controller-manager
# will patch controller-manager flags once restart completes to lower QPS/BURST
```

maria: After scaling to 1 replica watch_queue_depth dropped ~50% in ~90s. Still seeing etcd leader change around 01:20 UTC and follower lag blips.

kai: Check etcd node disk_iops and whether compaction or snapshots overlapped with the migration window. Those IO spikes will amplify follower lag.

oliver: I see etcd node disk iops in eu-west peaked ~01:18 UTC. Backup job + compaction likely overlapped the migration surge.

tessa: I temporarily disabled the scheduled backup for eu-west and pinged infra-backups for a delayed window.

maria: @sre-bot current status?

sre-bot: Cluster health summary: apiserver=Degraded, etcd=Degraded (follower_lag_high), controller-manager=Degraded (queue_length_high). Active alerts throttled for 10m to reduce alert noise.

kai: Action plan:
- Pause live GPU migration pipeline immediately
- Keep provisioner at 1 replica until watch queue stabilizes
- Delay backups/compaction in eu-west for 30m window
- If we don't see normalization, prepare traffic failover to eu-central (exec signoff required due to egress cost/latency)
- Postmortem to weigh reserved_warm_pool vs frequent live moves (cost vs reliability)

oliver: Note on failover: cross-region attach/egress adds latency and cost. Need product/exec signoff before cutover.

tessa: I raised a PR to flip the migration pipeline pause; awaiting approvals. If approved I'll flip in ~5m.

maria: Monitoring shows improvement after scaling down provisioner and pausing backups. Will observe for 20m and post updates here. :eyes:

oliver: For the postmortem, recommend evaluating a small reserved warm GPU pool in eu-west to reduce attach churn. More expensive, but predictable. Also consider staggering compaction/snapshots across etcd members to avoid simultaneous IO spikes.

maria: Captured artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-ops/apiserver-eu-gpu-migrate-6767012345 (metrics, logs, traces).

kai: I'll draft a short incident summary + postmortem template after we stabilize. Thanks for quick ops on throttling. :thumbsup:
